title: Slut med nakenbad på Kallis under ”mixdagarna”
content:
Första måndagen varje månad samt varje tisdag mellan 7 och 9 är det mixdag på Kallis. Det innebär att vem som helst kan byta om och vistas var han, hon eller hen vill. Efter flera månaders diskussioner har nu ledningen för Kallis beslutat att under de så kallade mix-dagarna/timmarna måste alla gäster ha badkläder på sig.
Måndag den 7 september träder de nya reglerna i kraft.
Annons
– Vi får jättemånga mejl hela tiden, från företag och kompisgäng, som vill besöka oss, men de är inte helt bekväma med att vara helt nakna, säger Jonas Rincon-Dahlberg och fortsätter:
Annons
– Detta är ett sätt att möta upp det. Sen får vi göra en utvärdering och se hur det fungerar.
Redan 2018 slopades könsgränserna när Kallis införde en queer-dag. Det dröjde inte länge innan besökare började slå larm om män som beter sig gränslöst – inte minst queera personer har fått frågor om sina kroppar. Queer-Kallis blev så småningom mix-Kallis.
Hundratals Malmöbor skrev för drygt ett år sedan under ett så kallat medborgarinitiativ om att en dag på Kallis reserverad för queerpersoner.
– Den könsneutrala dagen är den mest straighta dagen som finns på Kallis nu. Politikerna hade kunnat hitta en lösning om de velat, sa Axel Repka, som startade namninsamlingen, till tidningen då.
Politikerna i fritidsnämnden avslog begäran om en ”separatistisk dag” på Kallis med hänvisning till lagen, men även rent praktiskt hade det varit svårt att fastställa vem som identifierar sig som vad, påpekade Jonas Rincon-Dahlberg då.
Alla inblandade sade sig då vara villiga att försöka hitta lösningar som skulle göra könsöverskridande bad möjligt och samtidigt minska risken för att vissa besökare skulle utsättas för obehagliga upplevelser.
Annons
Annons
I februari i år förlängde Malmö stad kontraktet med företaget Hekajo AB, som driver badet på kommunens uppdrag. Då startade också arbetet som landade i beslutet om kläder på, som fattades för en dryg vecka sedan.
– Vi har inget krav på oss att ha någon queer dag eller att det ska vara naket. Det kravet vi har från politiker är att det ska vara mixade dagar, säger Jonas Rincon-Dahlberg .

title: Los psicólogos coinciden: volver a ver películas o series que ya vimos está relacionado con la búsqueda del bienestar
content:
Encontrá las guías de servicio con tips de los expertos sobre cómo actuar frente a problemas cotidianos: Adicciones, violencia, abuso, tecnología, depresión, suicidio, apuestas online, bullying, transtornos de la conducta alimentaria y más.
Los psicólogos coinciden: volver a ver películas o series que ya vimos está relacionado con la búsqueda del bienestar
Si bien el catálogo de las plataformas se modifica a diario, muchas personas eligen historias que conocen de memoria; la nostalgia, la regulación emocional y la previsibilidad explican este fenómeno común en el público general
- 3 minutos de lectura'
¿Quién no vio una película o serie más de una vez? Más allá de que esto ocurre con las producciones que encabezan la lista de nuestras preferidas, los especialistas señalan que detrás de esta conducta existe un mecanismo psicológico profundo relacionado con el bienestar y el manejo del estrés.
En la era del streaming, donde las opciones son infinitas, el acto de volver a ver contenidos conocidos parece una contradicción. Sin embargo, la ciencia demuestra que esta práctica ofrece beneficios psicológicos específicos que la novedad no logra sustituir.
Un estudio clave publicado por Cristel Antonia Russell y Sidney J. Levy en el Journal of Consumer Research analiza el fenómeno del “reconsumo” de medios. Los investigadores descubrieron que volver a ver una película no es una simple repetición pasiva, sino una experiencia hedónica y reparadora. Según el análisis, las personas reobservan producciones para controlar sus emociones, procesar momentos de transición personal y reconectar con su propia identidad.
La previsibilidad de una trama ya conocida otorga un refugio mental inmediato. Cuando atravesamos períodos de fatiga o ansiedad, el cerebro busca minimizar el esfuerzo cognitivo. Una historia nueva exige atención constante, procesamiento continuo de datos e incertidumbre sobre el destino de los personajes. En cambio, una serie familiar elimina la carga mental del suspenso. Sabemos exactamente qué ocurre en cada escena, cuándo llega el conflicto y cómo se resuelve, lo cual genera una sensación de seguridad y absoluto control en un entorno cotidiano a menudo impredecible.
Este efecto se conecta directamente con la regulación emocional y la fisiología del descanso. La psicología indica que la familiaridad produce comodidad y reduce significativamente los niveles de cortisol, la hormona asociada al estrés. El espectador sabe de antemano qué emociones va a experimentar y en qué momento preciso van a surgir. Por ende, la elección de un contenido conocido funciona como una herramienta activa de autorregulación: si alguien necesita reír, llorar o sentirse tranquilo, recurre a una producción que garantiza ese resultado de manera inmediata y sin sorpresas desagradables.
Por otro lado, la nostalgia desempeña un rol fundamental en la construcción del bienestar psicológico. Las obras audiovisuales actúan como anclas temporales que nos vinculan con etapas específicas del pasado. Al revisar una serie favorita, la persona no solo reconecta con la ficción en sí, sino también con el estado psicoemocional que tenía durante el primer momento en el que reprodujo la ficción. Este viaje al pasado fortalece el sentido de continuidad personal, consolida la autoestima y brinda un espacio seguro de reconexión con valores, vínculos afectivos o momentos felices de la vida.
A diferencia del desgaste habitual que genera la repetición de otros estímulos, las producciones artísticas retienen su valor psicológico a lo largo del tiempo. Aunque la trama permanezca idéntica, el espectador cambia con los años. Al regresar a una historia en una etapa vital distinta, la persona descubre nuevos matices, reinterpreta los diálogos, identifica detalles inadvertidos y resignifica el mensaje original según su realidad actual. Así, la reobservación audiovisual se consolida no como una pérdida de tiempo, sino como un hábito saludable, profundamente rico en significado y fundamental para preservar el equilibrio mental.

Kibaha. Manispaa ya Kibaha, Mkoa wa Pwani, kuimarisha hatua ya upimaji na urasimishaji wa ardhi kupitia wataalamu wake ili kuharakisha upatikanaji wa hati za umiliki na kupunguza migogoro inayotokana na kutokuwa na nyaraka halali.
Hatua hiyo inakuja baada ya baadhi ya wazabuni waliokuwa wamepewa kazi za upimaji na urasimishaji kushindwa kukamilisha kazi hizo, hali iliyowaacha baadhi ya wananchi waliolipia huduma hizo bila hati za ardhi.
Akizungumza katika kikao cha Baraza la Manispaa ya Kibaha Agosti 19, 2026, Meya wa Manispaa hiyo, Dk Nicas Mawazo, amesema uamuzi huo unalenga kuhakikisha wananchi wanapata huduma za upimaji na urasimishaji kwa wakati.
Amesema awali manispaa ilikuwa ikiwatumia wazabuni kutekeleza kazi hizo, lakini baadhi yao hawakukamilisha kazi walizopewa, hali iliyochangia wananchi kukosa hati na kuongeza uwezekano wa kutokea kwa migogoro ya ardhi.
“Baada ya uhakiki kukamilika, shughuli ya urasimishaji itaanza ili kila mwananchi awe na hati na kunufaika na ardhi yake, huku Serikali nayo ikinufaika kupitia kodi ya ardhi,” amesema Dk Mawazo.
Amesema uhakiki wa wananchi waliotoa fedha kwa ajili ya urasimishaji lakini hawakupata huduma hiyo tayari umeanza na unatarajiwa kukamilika mwishoni mwa Agosti mwaka huu.
Kwa mujibu wa Dk Mawazo, hatua hiyo inalenga kuhakikisha wananchi waliokuwa wamesubiri kwa muda mrefu wanapata huduma walizolipia na kuwa na uhakika wa umiliki wa maeneo yao.
Amesema kuwa na hati za ardhi kutawasaidia wananchi kutumia maeneo yao kwa shughuli mbalimbali za maendeleo, huku Serikali ikiongeza mapato kupitia kodi ya ardhi.
Mkurugenzi wa Manispaa ya Kibaha, Dk Rogers Shemwelekwa, amewataka wananchi kushirikiana na wataalamu wa ardhi katika shughuli hiyo ili ikamilike kwa wakati.
Amesema ushirikiano huo utasaidia kutoa taarifa sahihi kuhusu maeneo, kutambua wamiliki halali na kurahisisha mchakato wa upimaji na urasimishaji.
Baadhi ya wananchi wameeleza kufurahishwa na hatua hiyo, huku wakitaka manispaa kuhakikisha utekelezaji wake unakwenda sambamba na ahadi zilizotolewa.
Charles John amesema uamuzi huo umewapa matumaini wananchi waliokuwa wakingojea huduma hiyo kwa miaka kadhaa.
Amesema anafurahishwa na hatua ya manispaa kuanza kushughulikia changamoto hiyo, lakini ameitaka ifuatwe na vitendo ili wananchi waliolipia huduma wapate haki zao.
Naye Anitha John amesema upimaji na urasimishaji wa ardhi ni muhimu kwa sababu humpa mwananchi uhakika wa umiliki na kumwezesha kutumia ardhi yake kwa shughuli za maendeleo.

title: Cashless payment services for children growing in Japan
content:
They are also attracting attention as a financial education tool that helps children learn how to manage their allowances and spend money systematically as Japan becomes increasingly cashless.
In July, Seven Bank began offering a prepaid card and a dedicated app for children aged 6 or older. Parents can load their children's allowance onto the card via the app and review their spending history.
Notifications are sent whenever the card is used. The app has a feature to send money to children as a reward for achieving goals, such as completing chores.
"With cashless payments, it is difficult to realize that money is finite," a Seven Bank official said. The bank aims to help children develop decision-making skills by encouraging them to think about how to use a certain amount of money and earn rewards by completing tasks.
"We're happy if children become Seven Bank customers in the future (after using this app)," the official added.
Sumitomo Mitsui Card Co. has also introduced a prepaid card and a dedicated app called "Kazoku no Osaifu," which allows money transfers between family members and balance management.
Rakuten Card Co. offers a prepaid payment service for families via smartphones. Sony Bank issues debit cards that can be used by individuals aged 12 or older for shopping if the account belongs to a family member.

title: Hexapod-assisted limb salvage after talectomy: outcomes of tibiocalcaneal arthrodesis using the TL-hex system.
content: Severe talar destruction due to infection, trauma, avascular necrosis, or neuroarthropathy represents a major reconstructive challenge. Talectomy followed by tibiocalcaneal arthrodesis (TCA) is a limb-salvage option in selected high-risk patients, although optimal fixation remains controversial. Modern hexapod external fixators offer computer-assisted multiplanar control that may improve alignment and fusion after talectomy. The aim of this study was to evaluate the clinical and radiographic outcomes of talectomy followed by TCA using the TL-HEX system in a series of high-risk patients. A retrospective observational study was conducted between January 2020 and January 2024 including all patients who underwent total talectomy followed by TCA using a TL-HEX circular external fixator. Indications included talar destruction secondary to infection, avascular necrosis, post-traumatic collapse, Charcot neuroarthropathy, and aseptic loosening of total ankle arthroplasty. Primary outcomes were radiographic fusion and hindfoot alignment. Secondary outcomes included time to union, functional scores (AOFAS, EFAS), pain (VAS), complications, and patient satisfaction. Preoperative and final follow-up outcomes were compared using paired statistical tests, with significance set at p < 0.05. Thirteen patients (mean age 57 years) were included with a mean follow-up of 24 months. Radiographic fusion was achieved in 11 of 13 patients (84.6%) using the TL-HEX alone, with a mean time to union of 22.1 ± 3.1 weeks. Two patients required conversion to intramedullary fixation, both achieving final consolidation. Mean AOFAS score improved from 39.2 ± 10.8 to 74.1 ± 9.7 (p < 0.001), VAS pain score from 5.1 ± 1.2 to 1.4 ± 1.1 (p < 0.001), EFAS score from 3.2 ± 1.8 to 14.3 ± 3.8 (p < 0.001), and SF-36 PCS from 23.4 ± 2.6 to 38.6 ± 3.5 (p < 0.001). Mean final hindfoot alignment was 6.5° of valgus, and all fused patients obtained a stable, plantigrade foot without bracing. No postoperative strut adjustments were required in any patient. Patient satisfaction was high (84.6% satisfied, 15.4% partially satisfied, none dissatisfied). No deep infections, amputations, or neurovascular complications occurred. Tibiocalcaneal arthrodesis using a TL-HEX hexapod fixator appears to be a feasible limb-salvage strategy after talectomy in selected high-risk patients, achieving satisfactory fusion, alignment, and functional improvement in our cohort. title: Ahead of festive season, Delhi Food Safety department destroys 131 kgs of expired food articles
content:
Delhi’s Food Safety Department identified and destroyed over 131 kgs of expired food articles, including besan, khoya, and atta, during an inspection, officials said on Thursday.
Ahead of Raksha Bandhan and Janmashtami, surprise inspections were conducted on Wednesday at sweet manufacturing units in Okhla, Badli, Nihal Vihar, and Narela, as well as at mandis, including Okhla Subzi Mandi and Ghanta Ghar Subzi Mandi. The drive comes ahead of Raksha Bandhan and Janmashtami festivals.
The Food Safety teams also collected 37 samples of paneer, khoya, ghee, sweets and other food products under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. These samples will be sent to designated food testing laboratories for quality analysis, and further necessary action will be taken based on the laboratory findings and in accordance with the applicable provisions of law, the department said.
Earlier this week, 508 kgs of spurious paneer was seized during an inspection at Okhla Sabzi Mandi by the department.
Health Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh has directed the Department of Food Safety to intensify inspection, surveillance and enforcement activities across Delhi.
“The health and safety of Delhi’s citizens is our foremost priority. With festive demand increasing, we have directed the Food Safety Department to maintain heightened vigilance across the city and ensure rigorous inspections and sampling. Special attention is being given to milk and milk products, sweets and other high-demand food items,” Mr. Singh had said.
The Health Minister reiterated that strict action will be taken against persons found involved in the manufacture, storage, distribution or sale of unsafe or adulterated food products. He appealed to all stakeholders to cooperate with enforcement teams and contribute towards ensuring safe and wholesome food for the citizens of Delhi during the festive season.
“Anyone found adulterating food items or compromising with prescribed food safety standards will not be spared. The health and safety of Delhi’s citizens is non-negotiable. Strictest possible action will be taken against those found endangering public health through the sale or distribution of adulterated or unsafe food,”Mr. Singh said.

title: BRIN finds "kelekak" forests speed tin mine ecosystem recovery
content:
"Kelekak forests near unconventional tin mines benefit ecosystem recovery in the area," Rozza Tri Kwatrina, a BRIN landscape ecology researcher, told participants of an online discussion entitled "Reshaping the Future of Kelekak in Bangka Belitung" on Thursday (August 20).
Recovery of former mining pits, known locally as kolong, is linked to improving water quality and changes in plankton communities, she said.
The communities shift from predominantly acidophilic organisms, such as Chlorella, she added, to more diverse groups, including Fragilaria, Amphora, and rotifers.
"Organic matter from kelekak forests provides a major food source for functional microorganisms, including sulfate-reducing plankton and local bioremediators, such as Amphora," Kwatrina said.
Related news: BRIN quake-resistant homes stand after 7.7-magnitude quake
Phytoplankton actively cleans the former mining pits by converting toxic heavy metals into solid sulfide compounds that settle harmlessly in the sediment.
"The proximity of kelekak forests ensures a constant supply of organic matter, scientifically accelerating natural pit recovery from hundreds of years to just several decades," she said.
BRIN studies found soil temperatures in kelekak forests ranged from 28 to 29 degrees Celsius, indicating a healthy microclimate.
"Dense kelekak trees, including durian, pelawan, cempedak, and mangosteen, effectively filter sunlight, keeping the soil moist and warm to support roots and soil microbes," Kwatrina noted.

title: Prime minister: As a nation, we are now wealthier than ever before
content:
Prime minister: As a nation, we are now wealthier than ever before
Estonia is free, secure and rapidly developing, Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) said on Thursday, marking the 35th anniversary of the restoration of independence.
Michal made the speech which follows at the flag‑raising ceremony on Toompea on the morning of August 20, reflecting on Estonia's journey from occupation to a respected nation and highlighting the country's economic and social progress over three and a half decades.
Thirty-five years ago we managed to throw off the shackles of occupation all together. At that moment, we had little to lean on. We did not know whether the freedom would last. But we had a strong will and a clear sight—the ambition to live in freedom, decide our own future, and build Estonia into a better place for all of us.
We turned our gaze in awe to the free world. The world where we so ardently wished to return to. To freedom, rule of law, and human dignity — the world where people can shape their own lives and futures.
But today we can raise our eyes and see that the world is looking at Estonia with respect. We are seen as a country that also shows the way for others. Estonia is considered one of the best places to live in this world. Our economic freedom and freedom of speech, smart ideas, respect for human rights, pure nature, and nurturing attitude towards the environment are constantly highlighted.
With three decades, Estonia's GDP has increased 15-fold and wages 60 times. Our life expectancy has been extended by more than 12 years — this is the biggest rise among the European nations. We are high up in the global ranking of countries with a very high level of human development. Our economy has grown on 14 years out of the last 17. Over the last two years, our economy has been growing again, as the most recent figures show.
As a nation, we are richer today than ever before. We have reason to be proud of our country and of how far we have come. We have reason to be hopeful about the future. Estonia is free, protected, and developing fast.
All this is based on the will and determination of the Estonian people. Our ability to build our home and our country. Our courage to make decisions that look beyond today or tomorrow, decisions that look decades into the future.
We have not walked this path alone. We have had good friends — and we cherish them. But at a crucial moment, 35 years ago, it was the people of Iceland who took the first step to support us.
Iceland's brave decision to recognize Estonia, which had only very recently restored its independence, was followed by other countries. I am sincerely happy to see the President of Iceland Halla Tómasdóttir among us today. The courage to be the first counts at historical moments. Estonia remembers it with gratitude.
Our goal must be that the Estonian flag is raised every day, forever, on top of Pikk Hermann Tower. We cannot stop working for this end. Freedom does not stay on its own. A country can never be fully completed.
The world is unpredictable, but our focus is clear. We know what we are protecting, treasuring, and where we want to end up. Our strength is a united, wise, and brave Estonian nation.
We need to take care of Estonia. We need to continue building Estonia. We need to make sure Estonia stays free. Long live free Estonia!

title: ‘First, donation must be to deity’: SC directs transparent system for Vrindavan's Banke Bihari Temple offerings
content:
‘First, donation must be to deity’: SC directs transparent system for Vrindavan's Banke Bihari Temple offerings
The court made it clear that donations must be deposited either through designated donation boxes or online into the temple treasury.
The Supreme Court has directed that every penny donated at the Shri Banke Bihari Temple in Vrindavan must first go to the deity’s funds, saying no person associated with the temple can appropriate offerings before they are deposited into the temple treasury.
Hearing a matter concerning alleged siphoning of donations at the temple, the court directed the committee overseeing its functioning to put in place a transparent mechanism to ensure that offerings made by devotees are properly accounted for.
The court made it clear that donations must be deposited either through designated donation boxes or online into the temple treasury. Any attempt by sevayats or others to obstruct the mechanism would be “viewed very seriously”, it said.
“First, the donation must be into the dedication, that is, to the deity, and from that you will get your share as part of the Bhandari duties,” the Supreme Court observed.
“You cannot appropriate [the money] before the devotee goes to the temple and gives the money into the deity's funds. It must be to the deity, and then you will get the share,” the court said.
Justice Bagchi, who was part of the bench hearing the matter, further remarked: “A priest cannot have a garnishee right on the deity.”
The observations came after an intervenor representing the deity submitted that money allegedly being taken by Bhandaris was actually cash received for bhog, or offerings of food to the deity. The counsel argued that the arrangement was protected by a decree of a civil court.
“That is a usufructuary right of the sevayats which has been recognised by a civil court decree, My Lords,” the counsel submitted.
The Supreme Court, however, emphasised that any share or entitlement of sevayats could arise only after the money had first been offered to and accounted for in the name of the deity.
The court also directed that any proposed purchase of property using temple funds should be brought before it before the transaction is concluded.
The directions are aimed at ensuring greater financial transparency in the management of offerings and temple funds, amid allegations of malpractices in the handling of donations at the prominent Vrindavan shrine.

“Furthermore, TB case detection in this region last year reached 112 percent of the estimated caseload, with a treatment success rate of 91 percent,” Deputy Minister of Health Benjamin Paulus Octavianus said on Sunday.
He attributed the achievement to an integrated service strategy and cross-sector collaboration.
One key factor behind the program's effectiveness is the use of portable X-ray equipment during CKG screenings, which helps accelerate the detection of lung disorders such as tuberculosis while also allowing screening for non-communicable diseases (NCDs), including hypertension and diabetes mellitus, Octavianus said.
“People with a history of hypertension and diabetes can be immediately treated and given medication, then continue their treatment at community health centers. If further treatment is needed, patients will be referred to hospitals,” he added.
As part of sustained support for the program, the Health Ministry has allocated 16 X-ray units through the 2026 State Budget for eight districts and cities in Banten that meet the required criteria.
In the same statement, Banten Governor Andra Soni said the provincial and district/city governments would continue working together to ensure the success of the CKG program and improve public health.
“Thank God, Banten Province has surpassed its target. However, we have set a higher goal, we want more than half of Banten’s residents to take part in the Free Health Check. Tangerang District has also exceeded 46 percent, with nearly 6 million Banten residents having undergone health checks,” the governor said.
Meanwhile, Tangerang District Head Moch. Maesyal Rasyid said his administration was ready to complete the remaining target through a proactive approach.
The CKG program in Tangerang is targeting 1.6 million participants and had reached 1.52 million. The remaining approximately 100,000 residents are expected to be covered in September through direct outreach to toddlers, older people, and pregnant women at integrated health posts (Posyandu).
Nationally, the CKG program is targeting 130 million participants in 2026. As of the latest data, approximately 82 million people had undergone the health checks.

title: Luminal Visualization versus White Swab Detection for Residual Contamination: A Single-Center Study at a Chinese Tertiary Hospital.
content: Residual contaminants in lumen-type medical devices pose infection risks. Conventional white swab detection has a limited detection rate, underscoring the need for a cost-effective on-site screening tool. In a single-center, prospective comparative study (Feb-May 2025), 1,100 cleaned orthopedic devices (500 intramedullary nails, 100 flexible bone drills, 500 others) were evaluated pre- and post-cleaning using a luminal visualization system and white swab detection. Outcomes included positive detection rates, time per item, material cost, and contaminant removal rate. Pre-cleaning, positive rates were 63.5% (698/1,100) for visualization vs. 18.9% (208/1,100) for swabs; post-cleaning, 35.2% (387/1,100) vs. 8.5% (94/1,100) (P<0.05). Median detection times were comparable (visualization: 34 s, IQR 20.0-44.0; swab: 32 s, IQR 16.0-38.0). Material cost was significantly lower for visualization (median 1.0 yuan, IQR 0.8-1.0) than for swabs (20.0 yuan, IQR 20.0-20.0) (P<0.05). Overall contaminant removal rate by visualization was 44.6%, highest for nails (68.1%) and lowest for drills (2.0%). Luminal visualization offers superior detection rates and significantly lower cost versus white swab detection, supporting its use for on-site screening of lumen device cleaning quality.

title: Diese drei Gemeinden im Raum Zürich sind für Familien am attraktivsten
content:
Diese drei Gemeinden im Raum Zürich sind für Familien am attraktivsten
Eine Studie zeigt, wo es sich für Familien mit durchschnittlichem Einkommen am besten lebt. Der entscheidende Faktor sind die Lebenshaltungskosten. In Aarau sind diese 28 Prozent tiefer als in Zürich.
Wer als Familie in der Region Zürich ein neues Zuhause sucht und über ein durchschnittliches Einkommen verfügt, der sollte seinen Blick über die Kantonsgrenzen hinaus richten. Das beste Verhältnis von Standortqualität und Lebenshaltungskosten bietet nämlich weder Zürich noch Uster oder Winterthur. Auf Rang eins steht Aarau, vor Baden und Schaffhausen. Die Stadt Zürich kommt an vierter Stelle.
Das ist das Ergebnis der neusten UBS-Studie zur Wohnattraktivität in verschiedenen Regionen der Schweiz. Die Bank hat untersucht, welche Gemeinden für eine Familie mit zwei Kindern das attraktivste Gesamtpaket bieten. Dabei hat sie unterschiedliche Kriterien berücksichtigt im Bereich Infrastruktur und Erreichbarkeit, Freizeit und Lebensqualität sowie Kosten.
Zürich hat viele Vorteile, aber verliert trotzdem
Für den Vergleich nimmt die UBS eine vierköpfige Familie mit einem Bruttoeinkommen von 150 000 Franken und einem Vermögen von 80 000 Franken, die zur Miete wohnt und 110 Quadratmeter beansprucht. Insgesamt fliessen 38 Variablen in die Berechnung ein. Sie reichen von den Reisezeiten zu Grosszentren über die Dichte von Läden, medizinischer Versorgung, Kitas und Schulen bis zu Gastronomie, Sportangebot, Grünflächen, Fluglärm und Kriminalität. Bei den Kosten berücksichtigt die UBS Mieten, Steuern und Krankenkassenprämien.
Das Beispiel Zürich zeigt, wie schwierig es ist, überall gut abzuschneiden. Bei Infrastruktur und Erreichbarkeit bekommt die Stadt in der UBS-Bewertung Bestnoten. Dasselbe gilt für Freizeit und Lebensqualität. Bei den Kosten hingegen fällt sie in die tiefste Kategorie. Das Leben ist hier im regionalen Vergleich sehr teuer, was die Gesamtattraktivität als Wohnort laut der Studie deutlich mindert.
Aarau schafft die attraktivste Kombination. Die Aargauer Kantonshauptstadt erreicht im Ranking bei Infrastruktur und Freizeit ebenfalls die höchste Kategorie, die Lebenshaltungskosten liegen jedoch im Gegensatz zu Zürich im mittleren Bereich. Baden ist ähnlich stark bei Infrastruktur und Freizeit, aber teurer als Aarau.
Das heisst natürlich nicht, dass Aarau oder Baden dasselbe bieten wie Zürich. Wer Wert legt auf eine Universität, internationale Konzerthäuser, Spitzengastronomie oder ein besonders breites Kulturangebot, findet davon in Zürich mehr. Für Familien zählen aber oft auch andere Dinge: gut erreichbare Schulen, Kinderbetreuung, Einkaufsmöglichkeiten, Sportangebote und kurze Wege. Gerade bei diesen Alltagsfaktoren können auch Mittelstädte sehr gut abschneiden.
Den entscheidenden Unterschied machen die Lebenshaltungskosten. Laut UBS liegen diese für die vierköpfige Beispielfamilie in Aarau um rund 28 Prozent tiefer als in der Stadt Zürich. In Schaffhausen sind es sogar 34 Prozent weniger.
Wenige Bahnminuten machen Tausende Franken aus
Dabei muss man gar nicht weit aus Zürich hinausfahren, um viel Geld zu sparen.
Eine vierköpfige Durchschnittsfamilie, die in einer Agglomerationsgemeinde mit 10 bis 15 Minuten ÖV-Fahrzeit von Zürich entfernt wohnt, gibt laut den Berechnungen der UBS für Miete, Krankenkassenprämien und Steuern im Durchschnitt rund 11 500 Franken weniger pro Jahr aus als in der Stadt. Ab einer ÖV-Fahrzeit von 45 Minuten wächst der Unterschied auf mehr als 20 000 Franken jährlich. Dieses Gefälle ist bei den anderen Grossstädten wie Bern, Basel, Genf und Lausanne weniger ausgeprägt.
Ganz gratis gibt es die Ersparnis allerdings nicht. Wer weiter ausserhalb wohnt und in Zürich arbeitet, nimmt längere Wege und damit zusätzliche Fahrtkosten und vor allem mehr Pendelzeit in Kauf. Die UBS berücksichtigt deshalb auch die Erreichbarkeit einer Gemeinde. Wie stark dieser Nachteil wiegt, hängt nicht zuletzt davon ab, wie häufig jemand tatsächlich zum Arbeitsplatz pendeln muss.
Mittelstädte als heimliche Gewinner
Die UBS verzichtet bewusst auf eine Rangliste für die ganze Schweiz. Denn rund 70 Prozent aller Umzüge finden in einem Radius von weniger als zehn Kilometern statt. Die meisten Menschen suchen ihren Wohnort also innerhalb eines bestehenden Lebens- und Arbeitsraums. Deshalb hat die Bank die Schweiz in zehn Regionen aufgeteilt und die Gemeinden jeweils nur innerhalb dieser Gebiete verglichen.
Eines der zentralen Resultate der Studie ist, dass mittelgrosse Städte häufig die Grosszentren schlagen. In neun dieser zehn Regionen landet eine mittelgrosse Stadt auf Platz eins. In der Westschweiz schlägt Vevey unter anderem Genf und Lausanne, in der Region Bern-Freiburg liegen Freiburg und Murten vor Bern. Nur Basel kann sich als Grosszentrum an der Spitze seiner Region halten.
Für Familien sind Mittelzentren oft attraktiver als Grossstädte
Das liegt daran, dass mittelgrosse Städte gross genug sind, um eine gute Infrastruktur sowie ein breites Angebot an Schulen, medizinischer Versorgung, Einkaufsmöglichkeiten, Kultur und Freizeit anzubieten. Gleichzeitig sind die Wohnungen und damit die Lebenshaltungskosten oft deutlich günstiger als in den Grossstädten.
Schaffhausen gelingt die Kombination «gut und günstig» besonders gut. Die Stadt schneidet bei Freizeit und Lebensqualität zwar etwas schlechter ab als Aarau oder Baden. Sie liegt in diesem Bereich aber immer noch über dem Durchschnitt. Gleichzeitig sind die Lebenshaltungskosten unterdurchschnittlich. Laut der UBS gibt es schweizweit nur vier Gemeinden, die das schaffen: Neben Schaffhausen sind das Altdorf, Estavayer und Appenzell.
Wer viel verdient, sollte anders rechnen
Allerdings gibt es den «attraktivsten» Wohnort immer nur für einen bestimmten Haushalt. Das gilt selbst für die hier untersuchte Gruppe der Familien. Ändert sich das Einkommen, verändert sich auch die Rangliste.
Für eine Familie mit einem vergleichsweise tiefen Bruttoeinkommen von 85 000 Franken bleibt Aarau in der Region Zürich-Aarau-Schaffhausen auf Platz eins. Dahinter folgen Schaffhausen und Baden. Zürich schafft es nicht einmal unter die ersten zehn. Stattdessen werden beispielsweise Olten, Zofingen, Uster, Greifensee oder Winterthur genannt.
Bei einem Bruttojahreseinkommen von 300 000 Franken pro Familie sieht die Situation plötzlich anders aus. Nun landet bei Familien Freienbach auf Rang eins, vor Lachen und Rapperswil-Jona. Zürich belegt wieder Platz vier, Rüschlikon Platz fünf, Zollikon Platz sechs und Kilchberg Platz sieben. Auch Küsnacht schafft es nun in die Top Ten.
Hier kommt ein anderer Faktor stärker ins Spiel: die Steuern. Je höher das Einkommen, desto stärker fallen tiefe Steuern ins Gewicht – und desto besser lassen sich hohe Wohnkosten verkraften. Bei einem durchschnittlichen Einkommen hingegen frisst die teure Wohnung den Steuervorteil vieler Zürichsee-Gemeinden wieder auf. Die UBS kommt deshalb zu dem Schluss, dass sich steuerlich günstige Wohnorte für viele Haushalte erst bei sehr hohen Einkommen auszahlen.

title: Ärzte im Patientengespräch: „In Ihrer Brust tickt eine Zeitbombe“
content:
Vorschnelle Diagnosen: „Sie haben ein Magengeschwür.“ Dramatische Mitteilungen: „Wenn wir jetzt nicht gleich operieren, sitzen Sie in einem Jahr im Rollstuhl.“ Lebensverändernde Sätze, zwischen Tür und Angel dahingesagt: „Ihr Kind wird wohl nicht mehr gesund werden“ – Ärzte bringen nicht immer die nötige Sensibilität im Umgang mit Patienten auf. Gründe dafür sind oft Zeitmangel und ein Vergütungssystem, dass Diagnosen und Therapien weit besser bezahlt als die sogenannte sprechende Medizin. Auch gehört Gesprächsführung noch nicht an allen Universitäten verpflichtend zur Medizinerausbildung. Dabei ist schon seit Langem bekannt, dass ein gutes Arzt-Patientengespräch nicht nur das Risiko einer Fehldiagnose mindert, sondern auch Vertrauen schafft und damit die Heilung fördert. Am Klinikum Rechts der Isar der Technischen Universität München müssen Studierende drei Pflichtmodule in Kommunikation absolvieren. Andreas Dinkel, Leitender Psychologe und Lehrverantwortlicher der Klinik und Poliklinik für Psychosomatische Medizin und Psychotherapie, erklärt, worauf es im Arztgespräch ankommt.
Ärzte im Patientengespräch„In Ihrer Brust tickt eine Zeitbombe“
Lesezeit: 6 Min.
Es gibt gute und weniger gute Wege, wie Mediziner Diagnosen überbringen können. Aber wie teilen Ärzte am besten einen Krebsbefund mit? Wie können sie mit schwierigen Patienten umgehen? Und warum ist das überhaupt wichtig?
Interview von Martina Scherf

title: Nuoret seuraavat somevaikuttajien talousvinkkejä, mutta eivät luota niihin
content:
Jos takavuosina sijoitusvinkkejä jakoivat taksikuskit, nyt niitä jakavat erilaiset sosiaalisen median vaikuttajat. Varsinkin nuoret seuraavat aktiivisesti somevaikuttajien talousneuvoja. Tämä selviää nuorten talousosaamisbarometristä, jonka Jyväskylän yliopisto toteutti yhteistyössä finanssijätti OP Pohjolan ja Helsingin yliopiston kanssa.
Somevaikuttajien antamien talousvinkkien määrä on kasvanut räjähdysmäisesti, ja nuoret seuraavat heitä ahkerasti.
– Somevaikuttajat, jotka antavat erilaisia talousvinkkejä, ovat erittäin merkittävä taloustiedon lähde. Nuoret seuraavat heitä äärimmäisen paljon, Jyväskylän yliopiston sosiologian professori Terhi-Anna Wilska kertoi Ylen Aamun haastattelussa.
Huojentavaa on kuitenkin se, että nuorten kriittisyys on säilynyt. Wilskan mukaan nuoret eivät luota kovinkaan paljon somen talousvaikuttajiin.
– Huomattavasti enemmän luotetaan omaan perheeseen, lähipiiriin, kouluun ja pankkeihin, Wilska sanoi.
Pikarikastumisneuvoja somessa
Somessa on runsaasti epärealistisia sisältöjä, jotka tähtäävät nopeaan rikastumiseen. Professorin mukaan osa sisällöistä voi olla jopa vahingollisia. Sijoitusneuvonta on luvanvaraista toimintaa, mutta somessa annettavat vinkit eivät kuulu valvonnan piiriin. Wilska vaatii tiukempaa sääntelyä nuorille kohdistettavalle markkinoinnille ja sisällöille sosiaalisessa mediassa.
– Pitäisi ehdottomasti pystyä jotenkin kontrolloimaan sitä, minkälaista sisältöä nuorille saa kohdentaa somessa ja miten lapsille ja nuorille markkinoidaan somessa, Wilska sanoi.
– Lainsäädäntökin on hiukan jäänyt jälkeen tässä, kun tekoälypohjainen kohdentaminen on kehittynyt niin nopeasti, Wilska lisäsi.
Professorin mukaan digitaalinen talousosaaminen onkin entistä tärkeämpää nykypäivänä.
– Olisi todella paljon syytä kiinnittää huomiota nimenomaan nuorten digitaaliseen talousosaamiseen, joka on entistä tärkeämpi talousosaamisen muoto, mitä tarvitaan varsinkin nyt tekoälyn aikakaudella, hän sanoi.
Some vaikuttaa nuorten ostoksiin
Nuorilta kysyttiin talousbarometrissä muun muassa korkolaskuun ja inflaation ymmärtämiseen liittyviä kysymyksiä.
Nuorten talousosaaminen on pysynyt vakaalla tasolla ja on yleisesti ottaen hyvä. Kuluttajakäyttäytymisen saralla on vielä parannettavaa.
Barometrissa kolmasosa kokee somen sisällön ohjaavan ostoksiaan. Somen vaikutus kuluttamiseen jakautuu sukupuolen mukaan: tytöistä 20 prosenttia kertoo ostaneensa hetken mielijohteesta somesta, pojista 10 prosenttia.
Somesuositukset saavat tytöt ostamaan useammin ja somen luoma varallisuuspaine koskettaa tyttöjä enemmän. 45 prosenttia kertoi, että ihailee ihmisiä, joilla on kalliit asunnot, autot ja vaatteet.
– Mitä parempi talousosaaminen nuorilla oli, niin sitä vähemmän alttiita he olivat somen ostoimpulsseille, sosiologian professori Terhi-Anna Wilska kertoi.

title: The effect of hawthorn vinegar, black mulberry syrup, and green tea on oral mucositis and oral health-related quality of life in individuals with diabetes: a single-blind, randomized controlled trial
content: ObjectiveThis study was designed as a single-blind randomized controlled trial to investigate the effects of hawthorn vinegar, black mulberry syrup, and green tea on oral mucositis and quality of life related to oral health in individuals with diabetes.MethodsTotal of 120 participants were divided into four groups (hawthorn vinegar, black mulberry syrup, green tea, control; n = 30 each) and the study was completed. All participants completed the “Patient Information Form,” “Oral Assessment Guide (OAG/ADR),” and “Oral Health-Related Quality of Life Scale (OHQoL-UK)” before the study, on the 7th day, and after the study. In the experimental groups (hawthorn vinegar group, black mulberry syrup group, green tea group). In addition to routine oral mucositis treatment, patients with DM gargled for 1 min with diluted hawthorn vinegar [1 tablespoon (10 cc) mixed with 40 cc of water], pure black mulberry syrup, or green tea solution three times a day for 14 days, 15–20 min before meals.ResultsPatients in the hawthorn vinegar group showed a decrease in oral mucositis and an increase in oral health-related quality of life at the interim measurement (day 7) and final test (day 14) measurements (p < 0.05). A negative correlation was found between the severity of oral mucositis and quality of life (p < 0.05).ConclusionAlthough there was no difference between hawthorn vinegar and black mulberry syrup, they were found to be more effective than green tea in reducing oral mucositis and improving oral health-related quality of life, and all three complementary treatments were found to be effective.Clinical Trial Registrationidentifier [NCT06481254]. https://register.clinicaltrials.gov/prs/beta/studies/S000E5O000000043/recordSummary.

title: Wo es trotz Konjunkturflaute noch Jobs gibt
content:
Arbeitslosigkeit und Strukturwandel Wo es trotz Konjunkturflaute noch Jobs gibt
Jahrelang kein Wachstum, das schlägt längst auch auf den Arbeitsmarkt durch. Hinzu kommt der Strukturwandel in der Industrie, der auch Arbeitsplätze kostet. Wo fallen Stellen weg - und wo gibt es neue?
Die Nachfrage nach Arbeitskräften in Deutschland ist auch im August schwach geblieben. Das hat der von der Bundesagentur für Arbeit monatlich ermittelte Stellenindex ergeben. Die Bundesagentur spricht von einer "Seitwärtsbewegung" auf dem Arbeitsmarkt.
Allerdings sei in immer mehr Branchen im Vergleich zum Vorjahr ein "leichtes Stellenplus" zu verzeichnen, vor allem im öffentlichen Bereich, dem Finanzsektor, der Energie- und Wasserwirtschaft sowie im verarbeitenden Gewerbe.
Unternehmen suchen Fachkräfte
Ein Blick auf die Karriereseiten großer Unternehmen zeigt: Fachkräfte werden gesucht. Siemens Energy sucht unter anderem Servicetechniker für Windkraftanlagen und Ingenieure, bei MAN sind Stellen für Mechatroniker, Elektriker und Servicetechniker ausgeschrieben. Auch kleinere Umwelt- und Energieunternehmen suchen Mitarbeitende.
Selbst der Anruf bei einem Heizungsbauer aus dem mittelfränkischen ländlichen Raum zeigt: "Wir brauchen Leute!" Weniger offene Stellen als vor einem Jahr gibt es dagegen laut Bundesagentur in der Gastronomie und im Bereich Information und Kommunikation.
Demografie sorgt für Lücken im Arbeitsmarkt
Allein der demografische Wandel sorgt für Lücken in Unternehmen und Betrieben. Eine Studie des Instituts der deutschen Wirtschaft (IW) kommt zu dem Schluss, dass der Renteneintritt der sogenannten Babyboomer den deutschen Arbeitsmarkt stärker treffen wird, als bislang befürchtet. Als Babyboomer zählen die geburtenstarken Jahrgänge von 1954 bis 1969.
Demnach erreichen bis 2036 im Schnitt jährlich rund 1,3 Millionen von ihnen das Rentenalter. Das wirkt sich auch beim mittelfränkischen Unternehmen Schotter- und Steinwerk Weißenburg aus. Einige Fachkräfte, die seit Jahrzehnten im Unternehmen sind, werden demnächst wegen ihres Alters ausscheiden, erklärt Geschäftsführer Jens Geiger. "Die kann man nicht von heute auf morgen ersetzen."
Pflege, Gesundheit und Erziehung, Handwerk und Bau
Besonders betroffen sind dabei - wie in den vergangenen Jahren auch - vor allem die Branchen Gesundheit, Pflege und Erziehung. "Hier gibt es weiter Bedarf, weiter unbesetzte Stellen. Aber auch im Handwerk, in vielen Verkaufsberufen, in der Gastronomie", sagt Bernd Fitzenberger, Direktor des Instituts für Arbeitsmarkt- und Berufsforschung (IAB).
Aber auch am Bau werden Arbeits- und Fachkräfte gesucht. Und manche Betriebe wollen sie auch selber ausbilden. Doch gerade das Baugewerbe und Kleinstbetriebe haben es dabei schwer, Stellen zu besetzen. Die kleinen Betriebe mit wenigen Beschäftigten finden sich vor allem im Handwerk. Gerade das Handwerk habe enormes Beschäftigungspotenzial, bescheinigt IAB-Direktor Fitzenberger der Branche. Allerdings sei das nicht immer populär bei jungen Menschen.
Rüstungsbranche mit deutlichem Plus
Während in der Automobilindustrie und bei deren Zulieferern Stellen abgebaut werden, zeigt eine andere Branche ein deutliches Plus bei den Jobangeboten. Rheinmetall mit seinem Sitz in Düsseldorf zählt dazu. Viele größere Rüstungsunternehmen sitzen aber in Süddeutschland, in Baden-Württemberg und Bayern. Die Renk Group mit Sitz in Augsburg sucht hauptsächlich berufserfahrene Fachkräfte, auch weitere Unternehmen aus der Branche haben Stellen- und Ausbildungsangebote.
Allerdings ist laut Ökonom Fitzenberger die Verteidigungsindustrie etwa im Vergleich zur Autoindustrie in Deutschland ein sehr kleiner Sektor. "Dort werden nicht alle Beschäftigten aus der Industrie unterkommen können, die jetzt ihren Arbeitsplatz verlieren oder die jetzt keinen Arbeitsplatz mehr finden", so der Direktor des Instituts für Arbeitsmarkt- und Berufsforschung.
Mobilität spielt eine Rolle
Nach Angaben des Arbeitsmarktforschers gibt es vor allem in den Metropolen ein Beschäftigungswachstum, vor allem im Bereich der Dienstleistungen und personennahen Dienstleistungen. Dazu zählen unter anderem die Pflege, aber auch das Handwerk. Wer auf Jobsuche sei, müsse auch einen Umzug in Kauf nehmen, sagt Fitzenberger. Doch das sei nicht immer einfach.
Als Beispiel nennt er die bayerische Landeshauptstadt. "Wenn günstiger Wohnraum fehlt, dann nützt mir natürlich ein tolles Jobangebot beispielsweise in München sehr wenig", sagt Bernd Fitzenberger. Zudem müsse auch der Partner oder die Partnerin einen vergleichbaren Job finden. Diesen Punkt wertet er als Hemmnis für ein Beschäftigungswachstum.
Hoffen auf den Aufschwung
Der für dieses Frühjahr erhoffte Aufschwung auf dem deutschen Arbeitsmarkt blieb auch aufgrund des Iran-Krieges aus. Dem Geschäftsführer des Schotter- und Steinwerks Weißenburg, Jens Geiger, fehlt derzeit vor allem die Planungssicherheit für den Betrieb. "Wenn ich weiß, was auf mich zukommt, dann kann ich auch meine Zukunft planen und dann kann man auch entsprechend investieren und neue Leute einstellen und ausbilden", sagt er.
Zuletzt haben Wirtschaftsinstitute positive Veränderungen registriert. Zum Beispiel hat das ifo-Institut eine sich bessernde Stimmung in der Exportwirtschaft festgestellt. Auch das Deutsche Institut für Wirtschaftsforschung (DIW) in Berlin sieht Anzeichen, dass die Lage sich bessern könnte. "So langsam scheint die deutsche Wirtschaft aber Fuß zu fassen", sagte DIW-Konjunkturchefin Geraldine Dany-Knedlik.
Doch bis sich das auf dem Arbeitsmarkt niederschlägt, dauert es immer einige Zeit. Denn dieser reagiert immer zeitverzögert auf die Entwicklungen in der Wirtschaft.

title: Realizaron sesión educativa en materia nutricional con pacientes insulinodependientes de Carúpano
content:
Pacientes diabéticos insulinodependientes del municipio Bermúdez, en el estado Sucre, participaron en una sesión educativa organizada por la Farmacia Comunitaria Simón Bolívar, con el propósito de aportarles hábitos saludables en materia nutricional.
Gloria Farías, coordinadora de la dependencia, informó que a la actividad se sumaron 25 participantes, entre pacientes, familiares y personal de la dirección de Gestión Social de la Policía Nacional Bolivariana y del ministerio de Obras Públicas, en cuya sede se realizó la charla.
La sesión abordó la importancia de la alimentación para los pacientes insulinodependientes, todos en la base de datos de la dependencia.
Destacó que es importante que los pacientes tengan sus medicamentos, pero también que entiendan que pueden y que no pueden hacer en materia de alimentos.
La sesión educativa fue dirigida por la nutricionista Dayana Gil, coordinadora del Banco de Leche Humana de la maternidad Candelaria García.
Durante la actividad, se les explicó cuáles son los nutrientes básicos que deben consumir y cuáles deben evitar.
Destacó Farías que se trata de atender a una población altamente vulnerable y que puedan sentir que con las herramientas adecuadas pueden tener una mejor calidad de vida.
Sucre / Yumelys Díaz

title: „Dásamlegt að heyra í nemendum aftur í húsinu“
content: Skólahald hófst að nýju í grunnskólanum í Grindavík í dag. Skólinn var settur í morgun.„Það var mikil gleði og góð stemning í morgun og það var alveg dásamlegt að heyra í nemendum aftur í húsinu,“ segir Guðlaug Erlendsdóttir, skólastjóri leik- og grunnskóla Grindavíkur. Leikskólastarf hófst fyrr í mánuðinum.Hún segir undirbúninginn hafa verið strembinn og starfsfólk hlakkað mikið til að skólastarf hefðist.„Þetta er svona toppurinn hjá okkur, eftir alla vinnuna sem er búið að leggja í þetta. title: 'It's a big step up': Behind the scenes as Netflix hit Dept Q returns to Edinburgh
content:
'It's a big step up': Behind the scenes as Netflix hit Dept Q returns to Edinburgh
- Published
Walking onto any TV set is a thrill - and having followed Department Q since Jussi Adler Olsen's novels were first developed into a Netflix series, the chance to visit the sound stages of Edinburgh's FirstStage Studios was even more thrilling.
The second season began filming in the Scottish capital in June, and is due to continue until October.
I was given the chance to go behind the scenes and speak to some of those behind the success of Dept Q.
The set includes maverick detective Carl Morck's New Town flat. It's four times the size of any actual property so it can accommodate the cameras, lights and crew, as well as the characters who are supposed to live there.
The attention to detail is extraordinary, from the half full jars of jam on the kitchen surfaces to the takeaway menus and personal trainer ads on the side of the fridge.
Elsewhere, a steep flight of gloomily-lit stairs lead to the basement where Morck and his misfits are based – the abandoned shower quarter of the fictional police station which gives them the name Department Q.
There are showers, and some of the most disgusting-looking toilets I've seen since Trainspotting - perhaps a homage to Leith's other great cultural export. Everything looks as if the characters have simply stepped out for a moment.
The biggest set is the interior of the police headquarters – an open-plan office with personal effects on each of the desks and boards of photographs and details of the fictional cases they're working on.
Inside the office of Det Ch Supt Moira Jacobson (Kate Dickie) there are even more files, including the cold cases she passes to the team in the basement.
There's a bravery award in her name on the wall, and a peek in her diary reveals a series of appointments, meetings and to-do lists.
The concrete pillars and swirling sixties carpets look like they could be part of the brutalist Argyle House building in the city centre which doubles as the exterior of their headquarters – but they've all been built from scratch.
The only headache for executive producer Rob Bullock is that the actual building is now earmarked for demolition.
"I am very sad that I've had to sign up to very stringent anti-bribery rules through my employment at Sony, because otherwise I would be down there with a suitcase of money begging them not to demolish this building - because it IS department Q," he jokes.
The building's future is secure until at least 2033, when the current lease runs out – but with 10 books in the series, the production team isn't taking any chances.
They've already begun scanning the building in case a digital recreation is required.
It's all part of the framework which American showrunner Scott Frank started to build when he persuaded Netflix to locate the show in Scotland three years ago.
Although there were Danish versions of several Department Q books, he was keen to make the first big-budget English language version.
He was working on another Netflix show, the Queen's Gambit, in Berlin when discussions first began about possible UK locations.
Edinburgh - with its varied locations, crew base, and studio space – was already top of the list. Then he saw it in person.
"The first thing he said when he got off the bus on the Royal Mile was: 'I love this place, we're going to film here'," recalls Bullock.
Other commitments meant Frank could only direct the first few episodes, but this time round he'll direct them all.
"He has a real love of British detective shows like Cracker and Prime Suspect so he's always wanted to do his own version of that," says Bullock.
"And for all his many awards and achievements, he's never had a second season of a show so I think this was an opportunity to see what that felt like."
The new series is based on Disgrace, the second in the series of books about a group of privileged men in the top echelons of society who are involved in evil activities.
Bullock says the second series is "much more ambitious and much more cinematic".
"We had about 60 locations in the first season. In this one, we are well over 100, travelling all around Scotland.
"We are also doing these great big ambitious stunt set pieces. It's a big step up."
The central role of Carl Morck is once again played by Matthew Goode.
Is he as grumpy and as irascible as he was in the first season?
"I don't want to give too much away but Carl maintains his standard of being pretty grumpy," he says as we sit at the kitchen table in his flat.
"It's actually everyone else who starts falling apart in season two and Carl comes across as remarkably restrained."
He says the Scottish setting and cast allow for an added strand of dark humour.
"There's intended humour that came across a lot in season one and then there's stuff that comes from characters and situations and how we play together as actors," he says.
"There's a gallows humour that goes within the medium that allows us to be shocked and our coping mechanism as an audience, and in life, is to laugh at things.
"And that's what makes it slightly different from some of the Scandi stuff which can be ultra bleak. So go Scotland."
Leah Byrne, who plays DC Rose Dickson, says the show is "very unashamedly Scottish".
"That means a lot of light and a lot of humour, but also a lot of darkness, which I think Scotland represents very well," she says.
She's also delighted to return to her character's trademark vivid curls and brightly coloured outfits.
"It's an absolute joy to come back and get a chance to give Rose another go.
"I think she's got so much under the skin that we're only starting to scratch the surface of."
She's one of a number of Scottish actors returning this season.

The show has also given work to a wide range of technical staff, as well as training for 60 young people via a scheme funded by Screen Scotland, Sony and Left Bank Pictures, Rob Bullock's production company.
"We were keen to find people who wouldn't usually come into the industry and give them exposure," he says.
"It's not just about actors and writers; it's about carpenters and electricians. People think of the television industry as an exclusive world but it's an industry that encompasses a lot of different skill sets.
"What's great is when you see young people come in on a month training scheme and then be hired back in for daily work."
Although they're only halfway through filming for season two, and it won't be seen on screens until next year, most of Department Q's recruits are keen to keep on going.
And with eight more books in the series, they're hopeful this is just the start of this Tartan Noir tale.
"I think all of us feel the same - that it is an utter joy of a job to walk into," says Leah Byrne.
"It's felt so easy in a lot of ways. If we went for 10 series, I think all of us would be more than happy to stick around for it."

title: Nieuwe betonnen balken Sainctelettebrug geplaatst
content:
Zaterdagmorgen omstreeks 9 uur hebben arbeiders de nieuwe betonnen balken van de Sainctelettebrug in Brussel geplaatst. De operatie vormt een belangrijke stap in de aanleg van het toekomstige Saincteletteplein.
Nieuwe betonnen balken Sainctelettebrug geplaatst
De liggers zijn elk 47 meter lang en wegen bijna 100 ton. Ze werden 's ochtends rond 7 uur per boot vanuit de regio Antwerpen aangevoerd en vervolgens met zware hijsapparatuur op hun plaats gebracht. De plaatsing van de balken vond plaats rond 9 uur.
De ingreep maakt deel uit van een groter project van Brussel Mobiliteit om de bruggen aan het Saincteletteplein te verbreden. Daardoor moet boven het kanaal een volwaardige openbare ruimte ontstaan, met meer plaats voor voetgangers en fietsers. Dit in het kader van de aanleg van meer open ruimte aan het hele Brusselse kanaal.
Ruimte op mensenmaat
Volgens Brussels minister van Mobiliteit Elke Van den Brandt (Groen) moet de vernieuwde inrichting een belangrijk verkeersknelpunt aanpakken en tegelijkertijd ook ruimte "op mensenmaat" creëren voor voetgangers, fietsers en trams.
De werkzaamheden brengen dit weekend wel verkeershinder met zich mee. Van donderdag 13 tot en met zondag 16 augustus verloopt het verkeer op het Sainctelettplein richting Rogier tijdelijk over één rijstrook. In de tegenovergestelde richting wordt het verkeer omgeleid via de Willebroekkaai, de Scheepswerfbrug en de Havenlaan. Ook de verbinding tussen de Negende Linielaan en het Saincteletteplein is tijdelijk afgesloten.
Daarnaast wordt tijdens de hijswerken ook de scheepvaart op het kanaal stilgelegd. Vanaf 16 augustus kan het verkeer opnieuw in beide richtingen doorstromen.
De herinrichting van de openbare ruimte rond Sainctelette loopt nog door tot eind 2027.

content:
Taiwan International Ports Corp (TIPC) said it has completed the installation of a smart harbor-entrance safety monitoring system, using artificial intelligence (AI) to monitor vessel movements at commercial ports across the country.
The system enhances the commercial port operators’ water safety management capabilities by replacing traditional port patrols with a proactive warning mechanism.
Maritime and weather information from the Central Weather Administration are to integrate into the system, sharpening its capabilities to respond to disasters and emergencies.
Photo courtesy of Taiwan International Ports Corp
The Port of Kaohsiung has completed a proof of concept for an AI-powered occupational safety monitoring application for vessel loading and unloading operations, allowing them to identify risks in real time, it said.
The state-run commercial port operator has established an AI Promotion and Implementation Committee to ensure that all decisionmaking processes are driven by data.
Biofuel bunkering services would be launched at the Port of Kaohsiung during the second half of this year, it added, saying it is seeking operators to provide liquified natural gas (LNG) in line with CPC Corp, Taiwan’s schedule for completing and commencing gas supply from its LNG receiving terminal.

title: Healthcare localisation: Tripoli University Hospital conducts advanced Laparoscopic Surgery allowing patient to leave hospital within 23 Hours
content:
Tripoli University Hospital reported yesterday that, in a medical achievement reflecting the advancement of its laparoscopic surgery services, the Advanced Laparoscopic Surgery team in the Department of Oncology, Liver, and Pancreas Surgery, led by Professor Ali Al-Gallai, recently performed a successful laparoscopic repair of a congenital anterior diaphragmatic hernia, eliminating the need for open surgery.
Laparoscopic surgery, or keyhole surgery, is a minimally invasive medical procedure where a surgeon operates through small incisions using a specialized camera and thin instruments.
The hospital reported that the patient's condition showed excellent recovery following the procedure, enabling him to leave the hospital after 23 hours.
Demonstrates the effectiveness of the advanced surgical intervention
The hospital said this demonstrates the effectiveness of the advanced surgical intervention and the speed of recovery, achieved while adhering to the highest standards of medical care and post-operative follow-up.
This achievement, the hospital added, is part of Tripoli University Hospital's efforts to provide advanced surgical services, promote the use of modern laparoscopic surgery techniques, and continue training and developing a new generation of surgeons, thereby raising the level of expertise in specialized surgical fields.
The success of the operation confirms the importance of the integration of the medical team, as the cooperation between the surgical team, the anaesthesia and nursing team, along with the supporting departments and services, contributed to providing integrated care for the patient and ensuring the best treatment results.
The surgical operation is part of a series of operations announced by the hospital and comes as part of the Tripoli government’s policy to localise the provision of healthcare.
This saves the privately funded patient the inconvenience and cost of having the operation abroad. It also saves the state the cost of subsidising health treatment abroad.

title: Day in the Life: Nail Artist Nelssy Lazcano
content:
Nelssy Lazcano began doing nail art as a hobby during the pandemic as a way to pass the time. She bought a nail kit, started practicing on her mom and sister and soon realized that she had a natural talent. This didn’t come as a surprise to her, as she was creative when she was growing up, sketching animals, fashion designs and landscapes.
Lazcano was working as a manager for Top Golf in January 2020 when a fistula on her spine caused a T10-12 incomplete injury. She wasn’t able to return to that job post-injury and thought nail artistry could be a good new career.
She decided to take the chance and enrolled in a nail school in Aurora, Illinois, in 2021. Lazcano excelled through the seven-month program and has been a licensed nail technician for the last four years.
In a spare room in her house, Lazcano built a studio that suits her accessibility needs. With help from her dad, she built low shelving so she can reach all her tools independently. She has a table that raises and lowers to make it easier to work from her wheelchair. Her dexterity is unaffected by her injury, but she does have to brace herself with her left arm to stay balanced. She sees clients four to five days a week. They find her through Instagram and have traveled as far as two hours for her precise and intricate designs.
She specializes in hand painted nail art, combining abstract colors, unconventional designs and even 3D elements like charms and rhinestones. No two sets are the same and each is an original work of art on a half inch canvas.
Here’s what a typical work day looks like for Lazcano.
6:30 am: My alarm goes off and I start the morning by cuddling my dogs. I have a quick breakfast and then start my make-up routine. I get ready every single day, even if I’m not working. I just feel like if you look good, you feel good and you do good. I’m not me without my lip liner and gloss.
7:30 am: I head to my nail room and make sure everything is set up and my utensils are sterilized. I turn on my work phone, reply to emails and appointment requests, and check social media. Since most of my clients find me through Instagram, it is important that I post consistently and respond quickly.
8:00 am: It’s time for my first appointment. I put on all my gear that I wear to protect me from the dust and chemicals. I wear an apron that goes past my knees, goggles and a K95 mask. I also have my clients wear masks. I started doing nails during the pandemic, so it is second nature for me. The two extractors on my table help to suck up excess dust.
10:30 am: Client number two! Most of my appointments take between 1.5-2 hours, but they can go up to four hours depending on the designs. I specialize in gel nail enhancements, both with the natural nail or an extension. I also do European cuticle work, which is detailed and helps the manicure last longer. When I do nail art, I paint with a 9mm brush so it takes time and focus.
Today I have a fellow wheelchair user as a client. It can be tricky to find an accessible and open-minded nail spa, so I’m glad I can provide both. My house is step free to get in, I have an accessible restroom, and my table raises and lowers to accommodate different wheelchair heights.
This client is a quadriplegic, so I called before to ask questions about her dexterity and any limitations I should be aware of. Everyone deserves to have pretty nails and I want all of my clients to feel comfortable when they come to my studio.
12:30 pm: I take a short break, eat lunch and check emails again. I take this time to get out of my chair and stretch or use my standing frame. Sitting all day and doing nails takes a toll on my body, so I make sure to build breaks into my schedule.
1:30 pm: My last client of the day booked a “freestyle set,” which is one of my most popular services. The client picks the colors, length and shape, but I choose everything else. I always include intricate art in my freestyles. That’s what I’m known for!
I set aside time to come up with the design in advance. Sometimes when they’re in my chair I’ll switch a couple of things up, but I like to have an idea.
I love designs with colors that pop or colors that don’t necessarily go together, but once they’re combined a certain way, it just works. I love designs that are unconventional. One of my favorite things is when a client tells me, “I got so many compliments, nobody has these nails.” It’s an original work of art.
4:00 pm: I clean up my station and reset it for the next day. I turn off my work phone and close the door to my studio. I’m intentional about completely separating from work since I work from home and want to maintain balance and normal business hours.
4:30 pm: I have dinner and exercise. I do a low weight, high rep Pilates workout five times a week. It has helped with my shoulder strength and endurance in pushing my wheelchair.
5:30 pm: Tonight I’m heading to Chicago for a networking event. I love connecting with other nail artists, hair stylists and beauty creators to share stories and learn new techniques.
10:00 pm: I shower and like to unwind, whether it’s lighting a candle, relaxing music or journaling. My night routine is sacred, I don’t feel normal without doing some type of self-care and pouring back into myself. I feel like it is very important for anybody, no matter if you have a disability or not.
See Nelssy Lazcano’s work and book an appointment: instagram.com/nailsxnelssy

title: AskMyDoc: engaging, educating, and empowering global majority communities on health
content: Health inequities disproportionality affects global majority patients, due to socio-economic disadvantage. This leads to poorer health outcomes, in terms of morbidity and mortality. Community based interventions are ways by which to improve the health of these underserved communities. AskMyDoc is a charity that was founded in 2011, with the aim to engage, educate and empower ethnic minority communities. This paper aims to highlight the work of the organisation, reflecting on the highlights and challenges of breaking down barriers to health for global majority patients. AskMyDoc has engaged through delivery of multiple talks and workshops in local community spaces, providing discussions in multiple languages. It contributed to health literacy during Covid-19, through creation of over 200 videos relating to Covid-19 and cancer screening awareness. Collaboration with charities and health organisations has been key to the success of the work, as has developing medical students and resident doctors through the work. AskMyDoc has demonstrated the positive impact of grassroots health promotion and advocacy. Despite challenges of a sustained volunteer workforce and funding restrictions, it demonstrates a path by which to better serve global majority patients in the United Kingdom.

title: California could make Jewish an ethnic identity under groundbreaking new bill
content:
California could become the first state in the nation to consider “Jewish” an ethnic and racial identity, rather than just a religious affiliation.
A groundbreaking bill, which was recently approved by the State Senate and is awaiting a vote in the Assembly, would expand California’s legal definition of ethnicity “to include Jewish identity” in demographic data collection. In other words, state agency forms would need to include a “Jewish” category in questions that allow for voluntary disclosures of ethnicity or race.
If the bill, SB 1387, goes on to become law, this requirement would also apply to public entities ranging from public schools to unemployment offices to prisons. But the clock is ticking, as Monday, Aug. 31, is the final day of the year that California lawmakers can pass legislation. The governor then has until Sept. 30 to sign bills into laws or veto them.
The ethnicity legislation has been a priority among many Jewish groups across the Gold Rush state, who believe that Jewish peoplehood should be tied to far more than just religion, and that the law should reflect this unique relationship.
“When state law misrepresents us and puts us in this box of just a religion, there are a number of implications,” said David Bocarsly, CEO of Jewish California, an umbrella coalition for dozens of organizations that sponsored the bill.
Man behind bill has fought for Holocaust education previously
“As antisemitism continues to rise, part of that can be attributed to misinformation and misunderstanding,” Bocarsly added.
Proponents of the SB 1387 bill achieved a critical milestone two weeks ago when the State Assembly’s Appropriations Committee passed it to the Assembly floor, where a vote has yet to occur. If the Assembly approves the legislation, it then must return to the State Senate for a “concurrence” vote on amendments before heading to the governor’s desk.
The bill’s architect, State Sen. Henry Stern, is the son of actor Daniel Stern, known for his role as Marv the burglar in Home Alone. Stern, who has represented the Malibu region for the past decade, has been a driving force behind bills focused on fighting climate change and improving Holocaust education.
He co-authored the legislation with three Democratic lawmakers who, like Stern, are members of the California Legislative Jewish Caucus: State Sen. Ben Allen and State Assemblymembers Marc Berman and Josh Lowenthal.
California is currently home to about 1.2 million Jews, who make up the second biggest Jewish population nationwide, trailing behind only New York. And while these residents may have varying opinions on the legislation, the 43 federations, councils and other organizations that make up Jewish California have thrown their support behind it.
Citing data from the Pew Research Center, a statement from the coalition noted that more than 50% of American Jews describe ancestry and culture as the core of being Jewish, while only 36% choose religion. The passage of SB 1387, Bocarsly argued, would help the broader Californian population understand this reality.
“People will see that and continue to be reminded we’re not just a religious group that can be flattened into one kind of monolithic idea,” he said. “When we aren’t counted, it’s hard to be able to address and respond to issues.”
Advocating for data collection within a specific community is not without precedent in California.
Bocarsly pointed out that in 2024, members of the LGBTQ population pushed for the passage of a bill that required California health agencies to collect sexual orientation and gender identity information alongside other demographic data. A couple years before that, the state began disaggregating data on Asian and Pacific Islanders, by separating Asian, Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander groups.
Touching on part of the Jewish community, Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom last fall signed a bill that created a new demographic data category for Middle Eastern ethnicities, including Israelis.
“All of these groups, year over year, have shown why data is valuable and why advocating for more data is good for their community,” Bocarsly said. “We believe the same for the Jewish community.”
Marc Dollinger, a Jewish studies professor at San Francisco State University, believes that the emergence of SB 1387 stemmed from the spike in antisemitism that followed the Oct. 7, 2023 Hamas attacks on Israel.
“This is a way of placing antisemitism alongside the other ‘isms,’” Dollinger said.
He likened the state’s commitment to ending racism, sexism, homophobia and Islamophobia to fighting antisemitism, noting, “They need the data in order to be able to do that.”
This bill, which would take effect in 2030, would ban the disclosure of personal information and require the use of de-identification methods to maintain privacy. The data collection would serve to inform research initiatives, identify disparities and guide policy decisions, per the bill.
“This is aggregated data,” Bocarsly said. “No list of Jews, no registry, will ever be published.”
California's privacy laws will likely prevent misuse of data, expert maintains
Joshua Goldstein, a professor of demography at UC Berkeley, raised some concerns about potential privacy breaches, telling The Jewish News of Northern California that this kind of data is “often collected in a non-anonymized manner.” In other words, he explained, a respondent’s name might appear in an initial answer, only to be erased later.
Bocarsly disputed these fears, stressing that California’s “robust data privacy laws” forbid the publication of aggregate datasets when the number of respondents is insufficient, to ensure that their identities aren’t easily guessable.
Both the Bay Area and Sacramento chapters of Jewish Voice for Peace opposed the bill, with the former arguing that past attempts to distinguish Jewish identity from other ethnicities have led to “catastrophic” outcomes and that treating a religion as an ethnicity “is legally inconsistent and factually wrong.” The Sacramento chapter, meanwhile, warned that this “wrong-headed oversimplification of identity” could “exacerbate antisemitism.”
Proponents of the bill, however, argue that in this era of increased antisemitism, such legislation could bolster much-needed protections for Jewish Americans.
Austin Sarat, a professor of jurisprudence and political science at Amherst College, argued in a recent opinion piece that California should not only recognize Jews as members of an ethnic group, but also “redouble its efforts to combat antisemitism in the state.”
“The legislation’s impact will not be confined to the Golden State,” Sarat stated, adding that government officials and Jewish leaders nationwide will “need to keep their eyes on what is happening in California and be ready to deal with the ripple effects.”
Beyond the role Jewish demographic data could play in fighting antisemitism, Bocarsly also pointed out the practical benefits that access to such information could provide in sectors like education or healthcare.
For example, he explained, the data could help improve screening protocols for certain genetic issues, like Tay-Sachs disease or BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations, which have outsized impacts on Jewish communities.
“We don’t have the ability to study when people go into the hospital and are diagnosed with some of these diseases,” Bocarsly said.
Although SB 1387 would be the first law to mandate the inclusion of Jewish ethnicity in public data collection, Bocarsly cited other efforts that have ventured in a similar direction. In 2024, the Oregon Health Authority began gathering Jewish ethnicity data in an effort launched by a cancer researcher. Years before that, the Obama administration also started recognizing Jews as an ethnicity in the context of discrimination, Bocarsly added.
If the California bill does become law, Bocarsly expressed hope “that other states and hopefully the federal government would also follow suit.”
Dollinger, the San Francisco State professor, said that the bill’s advancement actually surprised him, observing that “in traditional Judaism, Jews do not count themselves” due to superstitions about the “evil eye.”
From a historical perspective, meanwhile, he pointed out that Jews have not fared well when “counted by governments.” A general distrust of authorities, Dollinger explained, has been a core issue for Jews as a vulnerable minority group.
“I’ve got to believe that Jewish leadership trusts the California state government to collect that data, and believe that collecting the data will help Jews,” Dollinger said.
Although he would not reveal his personal opinion on the bill, Dollinger said he is in favor of deeming Jewishness an ethnicity.
Doing so, he continued, has a history dating back to Wilhelm Marr’s coinage of the term antisemitism in 1879. Marr spoke of antisemitism in a racist rather than a religious context because he “considered Jews to be a subhuman race,” Dollinger explained.
In modern day America, Dollinger referred to Sen. Bernie Sanders, an Independent from Vermont, as “a classic example” of a “cultural Jew” who isn’t faith-driven but is recognizably Jewish to members of the public.
“Having Jews as an ethnic category is correct,” he confirmed.
The unique ethnic characteristics that they’ve developed around the Diaspora over time “are both particular to them as Jews and differentiating them as Jews from the communities around them,” Dollinger added.

title: Philadelphia neighborhood may finally get some flood relief
content:
Transcript:
In Philadelphia’s Eastwick neighborhood, heavy rain is cause for alarm.
Johnson: “If we’re looking outdoors and the rain is coming hard, everyone is in a panic.”
Lifelong resident Donna Johnson says during storms, water rushes in from upstream and fills the creeks in Eastwick.
It overflows the banks, flooding streets and homes in the low-lying area.
And the risks are growing as climate change causes more intense rain and rising seas worsen storm surge flooding from the nearby Delaware River.
For a long time, residents have pushed for the city to address the problem.
Johnson: “It took so long for this concern to be a concern of more than just the neighbors.”
But finally, momentum is building. The city has partnered with residents to develop a set of proposed solutions that was released this spring.
It includes building an earthen levee, improving stormwater drainage, creating a wetland park to absorb water, and offering buyouts to help people in the most vulnerable spots move to higher ground.
There’s a long road ahead to secure funding and implement the projects. But Johnson’s committed to keeping at it.
Johnson: “I love my neighborhood. … It’s home.”

title: A network optimization framework for fuel break planning in wildfire-prone landscapes: Accounting for fuel break failures and wildlife conservation goals
content: by Denys Yemshanov, Ning Liu, Eric W. Neilson, Daniel Thompson, Frank H. Koch, Kelsey Gritter Large wildfires are a dominant type of disturbance in North American forests that have caused significant environmental impacts and economic damages. A potential approach to mitigate wildfire spread risk is to segment the landscape with fuel breaks or similar areas with reduced fuel content. However, fragmenting the landscape may undermine other ecosystem services, such as the provision of wildlife migration routes. We present a mixed-integer programming fuel break planning model that minimizes wildfire hazard while protecting migration routes for an endangered wildlife species population (woodland caribou, Rangifer tarandus caribou). Our model applies the network optimization concept and minimizes the expected burn area in the landscape while protecting a target proportion of the wildlife migration routes. We depict the landscape as a network of patches with fuel and track the impact of fuel breaks across a large set of predicted fire spread scenarios where each scenario is conceptualized as a fire propagation graph. We formulated the fuel break allocation as a scenario-based, mixed-integer optimization problem and used the fuel break widths to track the potential failures of the fuel breaks to contain the fire spread. We also considered a planning problem that minimized the expected area of the largest fires and fuel connectivity in the landscape. For given fire hazard reduction goals, the optimal solutions are those with the least disruptive impacts on the wildlife migration routes. We implemented the approach for the planning of wildfire mitigation in the Red Rock-Prairie Creek area of Alberta (Canada), a fire-prone landscape with the presence of caribou populations. The proposed approach reduced the wildfire spread potential in the area with a trade-off of moderate impacts on known caribou migration routes. Such a methodology is timely to help develop strategies for reducing wildfire hazard in fire-prone forest landscapes while achieving conservation management goals in other regions.
